    23→## Platform-Audience Fit Matrix
    24→
    25→| Platform | Best For | Audience | Content Type | Posting Cadence |
    26→|----------|----------|----------|--------------|-----------------|
    27→| **LinkedIn** | B2B, thought leadership, career | Professionals, decision-makers | Long-form, insights, case studies | 3-5x/week |
    28→| **Twitter/X** | Real-time, tech, commentary | Tech-savvy, news followers | Short-form, threads, hot takes | 2-5x/day |
    29→| **Instagram** | Visual brands, lifestyle | 18-34, visual consumers | Photos, Reels, Stories | 1-2x/day |
    30→| **TikTok** | Gen Z, entertainment | Under 30, trend followers | Short video, trends, education | 1-3x/day |
    31→| **YouTube** | Long-form education, how-to | Research-intent audiences | Tutorials, vlogs, deep dives | 1-2x/week |
    32→
    33→## Platform Selection Scorecard
    34→
    35→Rate each platform 1-10:
    36→
    37→| Factor | Question |
    38→|--------|----------|
    39→| **Audience Presence** | Are your ideal customers actively using this platform? |
    40→| **Content Fit** | Does your natural content style work here? |
    41→| **Competitive Gap** | Is there room to stand out vs. competitors? |
    42→| **Resource Match** | Can you consistently create required content? |
    43→| **Business Alignment** | Does the platform support your conversion goals? |
    44→
    45→**Platform Score = (Audience × 2 + Content + Gap + Resources + Alignment) / 7**
    46→
    47→Prioritize platforms scoring 7+. Focus on 2-3 maximum until systematized.
    48→
    49→## Platform-Specific Strategy Deep Dive
    50→
    51→### LinkedIn Strategy
    52→
    53→| Element | Best Practice | Avoid |
    54→|---------|---------------|-------|
    55→| **Profile** | Headline = Value prop, not title | Generic "CEO at Company" |
    56→| **Posts** | Personal stories + professional insight | Pure corporate content |
    57→| **Hook** | First line is everything (pre-fold) | Burying the lede |
    58→| **Format** | Short paragraphs, line breaks | Wall of text |
    59→| **CTAs** | Ask questions, invite discussion | "Like and share!" |
    60→| **Timing** | Tue-Thu, 8-10am or 5-6pm | Weekends, late night |
    61→
    62→**LinkedIn Algorithm Signals:**
    63→- Dwell time (keep them reading)
    64→- Comments within first hour
    65→- Personal connections engaging
    66→- No external links in post (comment instead)
    67→
    68→### Twitter/X Strategy
    69→
    70→| Element | Best Practice | Avoid |
    71→|---------|---------------|-------|
    72→| **Bio** | Clear value + personality | Generic descriptions |
    73→| **Tweets** | Strong opinions, actionable tips | Safe, generic takes |
    74→| **Threads** | Hook tweet + numbered insights | Weak opener, no structure |
    75→| **Engagement** | Reply to bigger accounts thoughtfully | Spam replies, bot behavior |
    76→| **Timing** | 8-10am, 12pm, 5pm (audience TZ) | 1-5am |
    77→
    78→**Twitter Algorithm Signals:**
    79→- Replies and quote tweets
    80→- Profile visits after engagement
    81→- Likes from accounts you follow
    82→- Thread completion rate
    83→
    84→### Instagram Strategy
    85→
    86→| Element | Best Practice | Avoid |
    87→|---------|---------------|-------|
    88→| **Feed** | Cohesive visual aesthetic | Random, inconsistent style |
    89→| **Reels** | Hook in first 0.5s, trending audio | Slow starts, no captions |
    90→| **Stories** | Behind-the-scenes, polls, questions | Over-produced, sales only |
    91→| **Captions** | Value-first, CTA at end | Caption-less posts |
    92→| **Hashtags** | 3-5 relevant, mix of sizes | 30 hashtags, irrelevant tags |
    93→
    94→**Instagram Algorithm Signals:**
    95→- Saves and shares (most weighted)
    96→- Comments (especially conversations)
    97→- Reel watch time and replays
    98→- Story engagement and replies
    99→
   100→### TikTok Strategy
   101→
   102→| Element | Best Practice | Avoid |
   103→|---------|---------------|-------|
   104→| **Hook** | Pattern interrupt in 0.5-1s | Slow intros, "Hey guys" |
   105→| **Format** | Native style, authentic | Over-produced, scripted feel |
   106→| **Trends** | Adapt trends to niche | Force-fitting, ignoring trends |
   107→| **Duration** | Match to content (7s-3min) | Padding for length |
   108→| **Text** | On-screen captions essential | Audio-dependent content |
   109→
   110→**TikTok Algorithm Signals:**
   111→- Watch time % (most important)
   112→- Replays and rewatches
   113→- Shares (highest weight)
   114→- Comments with keywords
   115→
   116→# Engagement Metrics Framework
   117→
   118→## The REACH Metrics Model
   119→
   120→| Metric | Definition | Why It Matters |
   121→|--------|------------|----------------|
   122→| **R**each | Unique accounts who saw content | Awareness, top-of-funnel |
   123→| **E**ngagement | Interactions / reach | Content resonance |
   124→| **A**mplification | Shares, retweets, reposts | Organic distribution |
   125→| **C**onversion | Clicks, profile visits, follows | Action-taking |
   126→| **H**olding | Watch time, dwell time | Content quality |
   127→
   128→## Engagement Rate Benchmarks
   129→
   130→| Platform | Poor | Average | Good | Excellent |
   131→|----------|------|---------|------|-----------|
   132→| LinkedIn | <2% | 2-4% | 4-6% | >6% |
   133→| Twitter/X | <0.5% | 0.5-1% | 1-3% | >3% |
   134→| Instagram | <1% | 1-3% | 3-6% | >6% |
   135→| TikTok | <3% | 3-6% | 6-10% | >10% |
   136→
   137→**Engagement Rate = (Likes + Comments + Shares) / Followers × 100**
   138→
   139→## Engagement Quality Hierarchy
   140→
   141→Not all engagement is equal. Weight by business value:
   142→
   143→| Engagement Type | Value Score | Why |
   144→|-----------------|-------------|-----|
   145→| Share/Repost | 10 | Vouching for you to their audience |
   146→| Comment (substantive) | 8 | Active investment, conversation |
   147→| Save/Bookmark | 7 | High-intent, return value |
   148→| Comment (emoji/short) | 4 | Low-effort signal |
   149→| Like | 2 | Passive acknowledgment |
   150→| View/Impression | 1 | Exposure only |
   151→
   152→## Content Performance Analysis
   153→
   154→| Content Type | Track | Optimize For |
   155→|--------------|-------|--------------|
   156→| Educational | Saves, shares, comments | Actionable value |
   157→| Entertaining | Likes, shares, views | Emotional reaction |
   158→| Inspirational | Likes, saves | Aspirational connection |
   159→| Promotional | Clicks, conversions | Clear value + urgency |
   160→| Community | Comments, replies | Conversation starters |
   161→
   162→# Community Building Framework
   163→
   164→## The TRIBE Model
   165→
   166→| Phase | Goal | Tactics |
   167→|-------|------|---------|
   168→| **T**arget | Define ideal community member | Persona development, audience research |
   169→| **R**ecruit | Attract right people | Valuable content, strategic engagement |
   170→| **I**nvest | Deliver consistent value | Exclusive content, recognition, access |
   171→| **B**ond | Create connections between members | Discussions, collabs, events |
   172→| **E**mpower | Turn members into advocates | User-generated content, ambassadors |
   173→
   174→## Community Value Exchange
   175→
   176→Members stay when value received > effort to participate.
   177→
   178→| Value Type | Examples | Implementation |
   179→|------------|----------|----------------|
   180→| **Knowledge** | Insights, tips, strategies | Educational content series |
   181→| **Access** | Early info, exclusive content | Member-only updates |

1→# Specification: Social Media Strategy Audit for selfrules.org
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→This task involves conducting a comprehensive social media strategy analysis for selfrules.org, the personal brand website of Mattia Filippo De Luca, a Product Manager with 13 years of experience offering B2B professional services (consulting, brainstorming, PM mentorship). The audit will evaluate current social presence, identify the optimal primary platform, develop a 30-day content plan, and create a community-focused engagement strategy that prioritizes meaningful relationships over vanity metrics.
     6→
     7→## Workflow Type
     8→
     9→**Type**: feature
    10→
    11→**Rationale**: This is a strategic deliverable task that requires comprehensive analysis, framework application, and creation of actionable artifacts (audit report, content calendar, engagement playbook). While not a code implementation, it follows the feature workflow pattern of research → analysis → deliverable creation → validation.
    12→
    13→## Task Scope
    14→
    15→### Services Involved
    16→- **main** (primary) - Website analysis for social integration assessment
    17→- **social-media-manager skill** (framework) - Strategic analysis methodologies
    18→
    19→### This Task Will:
    20→- [ ] Analyze all current social media channels with quantified scoring
    21→- [ ] Evaluate bidirectional website-social integration
    22→- [ ] Identify and recommend the #1 priority platform with data-driven rationale
    23→- [ ] Create a 30-day cross-platform content calendar
    24→- [ ] Develop a community building engagement strategy (not follower acquisition)
    25→- [ ] Apply REACH metrics and TRIBE community frameworks
    26→- [ ] Generate actionable recommendations prioritized by impact/effort
    27→
    28→### Out of Scope:
    29→- Actual social media post creation (use copywriter-hybrid agent for that)
    30→- Social media account setup or configuration
    31→- Automated posting integrations or API development
    32→- Paid advertising strategy
    33→- Influencer partnership recommendations
    34→
    35→## Service Context
    36→
    37→### Main Website (selfrules.org)
    38→
    39→**Tech Stack:**
    40→- Language: TypeScript
    41→- Framework: Next.js 14 (App Router)
    42→- Styling: Tailwind CSS (Neobrutalist design system)
    43→- Key directories: app, components, lib
    44→
    45→**Entry Point:** `app/[locale]/page.tsx`
    46→
    47→**How to Run:**
    48→```bash
    49→npm run dev
    50→```
    51→
    52→**Port:** 3000
    53→
    54→**Relevant Sections for Social Integration:**
    55→- Homepage hero and CTAs
    56→- Blog section
    57→- Contact/Booking section
    58→- Footer social links
    59→
    60→### Social Media Manager Skill
    61→
    62→**Location:** `.claude/skills/social-media-manager/SKILL.md`
    63→
    64→**Key Frameworks Available:**
    65→- Platform Selection Scorecard (1-10 rating system)
    66→- REACH Metrics Model (Reach, Engagement, Amplification, Conversion, Holding)
    67→- TRIBE Community Model (Target, Recruit, Invest, Bond, Empower)
    68→- 4-1-1 Content Mix Rule (60% value, 25% engagement, 15% promotional)
    69→- Platform-specific strategy deep dives
    70→
    71→## Files to Modify
    72→
    73→| File | Service | What to Change |
    74→|------|---------|---------------|
    75→| N/A - Strategic deliverable | N/A | Create audit report document |
    76→
    77→**Output Deliverables:**
    78→| Deliverable | Format | Description |
    79→|-------------|--------|-------------|
    80→| Social Audit Report | Markdown | Comprehensive analysis with scores |
    81→| Platform Recommendation | Analysis | #1 platform with rationale |
    82→| 30-Day Content Calendar | Table/Schedule | Cross-platform content plan |
    83→| Engagement Playbook | Framework | Community building strategy |
    84→
    85→## Files to Reference
    86→
    87→These files provide context and frameworks:
    88→
    89→| File | Pattern to Copy |
    90→|------|----------------|
    91→| `.claude/skills/social-media-manager/SKILL.md` | Platform Selection Scorecard, REACH metrics, TRIBE model |
    92→| `.claude/skills/marketing-manager/SKILL.md` | AARRR Pirate Metrics, growth loops |
    93→| `.claude/skills/web-analyst/SKILL.md` | HEART framework for site integration |
    94→| `app/[locale]/page.tsx` | Website structure for integration analysis |
    95→| `CLAUDE.md` | Brand voice and content guidelines |
    96→
    97→## Patterns to Follow
    98→
    99→### Platform Selection Scorecard
   100→
   101→From `.claude/skills/social-media-manager/SKILL.md`:
   102→
   103→| Factor | Question | Weight |
   104→|--------|----------|--------|
   105→| **Audience Presence** | Are ideal customers actively using this platform? | 2x |
   106→| **Content Fit** | Does natural content style work here? | 1x |
   107→| **Competitive Gap** | Is there room to stand out vs. competitors? | 1x |
   108→| **Resource Match** | Can you consistently create required content? | 1x |
   109→| **Business Alignment** | Does platform support conversion goals? | 1x |
   110→
   111→**Score Formula:** `(Audience × 2 + Content + Gap + Resources + Alignment) / 7`
   112→
   113→**Threshold:** Prioritize platforms scoring 7+. Focus on 2-3 maximum.
   114→
   115→### REACH Metrics Model
   116→
   117→| Metric | Definition | Business Value |
   118→|--------|------------|----------------|
   119→| **R**each | Unique accounts who saw content | Awareness, top-of-funnel |
   120→| **E**ngagement | Interactions / reach | Content resonance |
   121→| **A**mplification | Shares, retweets, reposts | Organic distribution |
   122→| **C**onversion | Clicks, profile visits, follows | Action-taking |
   123→| **H**olding | Watch time, dwell time | Content quality |
   124→
   125→### TRIBE Community Model
   126→
   127→| Phase | Goal | Tactics |
   128→|-------|------|---------|
   129→| **T**arget | Define ideal community member | Persona development |
   130→| **R**ecruit | Attract right people | Valuable content, strategic engagement |
   131→| **I**nvest | Deliver consistent value | Exclusive content, recognition |
   132→| **B**ond | Create member connections | Discussions, collaborations |
   133→| **E**mpower | Turn members into advocates | UGC, ambassadors |
   134→
   135→### Content Mix (4-1-1 Rule Adapted)
   136→
   137→| Content Type | Percentage | Purpose |
   138→|--------------|------------|---------|
   139→| Value Posts | 60% | Educate, inspire, demonstrate expertise |
   140→| Engagement Posts | 25% | Questions, polls, discussions |
   141→| Promotional Posts | 15% | CTAs, offers, conversions |
   142→
   143→## Requirements
   144→
   145→### Functional Requirements
   146→
   147→1. **Social Presence Audit**
   148→   - Description: Comprehensive assessment of all existing social channels with quantified scoring
   149→   - Acceptance: Each platform rated using Platform Selection Scorecard (1-10 scale with weighted formula)
   150→
   151→2. **Website-Social Integration Analysis**
   152→   - Description: Evaluate bidirectional flow between website and social channels
   153→   - Acceptance: Document Site→Social and Social→Site integration points with effectiveness scores
   154→
   155→3. **Primary Platform Recommendation**
   156→   - Description: Identify the #1 platform to prioritize based on target audience fit
   157→   - Acceptance: Clear recommendation with data-driven rationale using scorecard methodology
   158→
   159→4. **30-Day Content Calendar**
   160→   - Description: Cross-platform content plan with specific topics, formats, and timing
   161→   - Acceptance: Daily/weekly schedule covering all recommended platforms with content types
   162→
   163→5. **Community Engagement Strategy**
   164→   - Description: Framework for building engaged community (not just follower acquisition)
   165→   - Acceptance: TRIBE model application with specific tactics for each phase
   166→
   167→### Edge Cases
   168→
   169→1. **Limited Social Presence** - If few/no active social accounts exist, focus on greenfield strategy and platform launch recommendations
   170→2. **Bilingual Audience** - Address Italian/English content split strategy for international reach
   171→3. **B2B vs B2C Balance** - Professional services audience requires LinkedIn-first approach but may benefit from broader reach
   172→4. **Time/Resource Constraints** - Solo practitioner means realistic, sustainable content cadence recommendations
   173→
   174→## Implementation Notes
   175→
   176→### DO
   177→- Apply Platform Selection Scorecard with actual scores for each platform
   178→- Use REACH metrics framework to define KPIs
   179→- Focus on community building (TRIBE model) over follower counts
   180→- Consider the B2B professional services context (consulting, PM mentorship)
   181→- Account for bilingual (IT/EN) content needs
   182→- Recommend sustainable posting cadences for a solo practitioner
   183→- Include specific LinkedIn strategy (primary platform for B2B)
   184→
   185→### DON'T
   186→- Recommend vanity metrics (follower count) as primary success measures
   187→- Suggest unsustainable posting frequencies
   188→- Ignore the professional/B2B nature of the target audience
   189→- Recommend platforms without clear audience-fit rationale
   190→- Create generic strategies without platform-specific tactics
   191→
   192→## Development Environment
   193→
   194→### Access Website for Analysis
   195→
   196→```bash
   197→npm run dev
   198→```
   199→
   200→### Service URLs
   201→- Website: http://localhost:3000
   202→

   204→- LinkedIn Profile: https://it.linkedin.com/in/selfrules
   205→- Website: https://selfrules.org (production)
   206→

   208→

1→# Platform Selection Scorecard Results
     2→
     3→**Subject:** Mattia Filippo De Luca (selfrules.org)
     4→**Audit Date:** January 26, 2026
     5→**Subtask:** 2-1 - Apply Platform Selection Scorecard to all candidate platforms
     6→
     7→---
     8→
     9→## Executive Summary
    10→
    11→After applying the Platform Selection Scorecard methodology to all five candidate platforms, **LinkedIn emerges as the clear primary platform** with a score of 9.0/10, significantly ahead of all other options. Twitter/X scores second at 6.4/10, qualifying as a secondary platform worth consideration. Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok all score below the 7.0 threshold and should be deprioritized.
    12→
    13→**Key Recommendation:** Focus 80% of social media effort on LinkedIn, 20% on Twitter/X for extended reach into the global PM community.
    14→
    15→---
    16→
    17→## Scoring Methodology
    18→
    19→### Platform Selection Scorecard Framework
    20→
    21→| Factor | Question | Weight |
    22→|--------|----------|--------|
    23→| **Audience Presence** | Are ideal B2B customers actively using this platform? | 2x |
    24→| **Content Fit** | Does thought leadership content style work here? | 1x |
    25→| **Competitive Gap** | Is there room to stand out vs. other PMs/consultants? | 1x |
    26→| **Resource Match** | Can a solo practitioner consistently create required content? | 1x |
    27→| **Business Alignment** | Does platform support consultation/booking conversions? | 1x |
    28→
    29→**Formula:** `(Audience × 2 + Content + Gap + Resources + Alignment) / 7`
    30→
    31→**Scoring Scale:** 1-10 (1 = Very Poor, 5 = Average, 10 = Excellent)
    32→
    33→**Threshold:** Prioritize platforms scoring 7+. Focus on maximum 2-3 platforms.
    34→
    35→---
    36→
    37→## Platform Scoring: LinkedIn
    38→
    39→### Score: 9.0/10 ⭐ PRIMARY PLATFORM
    40→
    41→| Criterion | Score | Weight | Weighted | Rationale |
    42→|-----------|-------|--------|----------|-----------|
    43→| **Audience Presence** | 10 | 2x | 20 | Perfect B2B fit. Decision-makers, PMs, product leaders ALL on LinkedIn. Italian B2B market has 70%+ LinkedIn penetration for professionals. Target segments (CTOs, CPOs, VPs, PMs) use LinkedIn daily. |
    44→| **Content Fit** | 9 | 1x | 9 | Thought leadership thrives here. Long-form articles, case studies, and professional insights are LinkedIn's core content. The "failure to success" narrative and pragmatic PM advice format is native to the platform. |
    45→| **Competitive Gap** | 8 | 1x | 8 | Moderate competition among PM consultants, but Mattia's unique positioning (design→dev→PM journey) and metrics-backed results differentiate. Italian PM thought leadership space is underserved vs. US market. |
    46→| **Resource Match** | 9 | 1x | 9 | Text-first content is manageable for solo practitioner. LinkedIn allows repurposing blog content, carousel creation from existing materials. 3-4 posts/week is sustainable. |
    47→| **Business Alignment** | 9 | 1x | 9 | Direct path to conversions. Professional context = appropriate for booking consultations. InMail for outreach. Company pages for credibility. LinkedIn profile can link directly to Google Calendar booking. |
    48→
    49→**Calculation:** (10×2 + 9 + 8 + 9 + 9) / 7 = **63 / 7 = 9.0**
    50→

1→# Platform Selection Scorecard Results
     2→
     3→**Subject:** Mattia Filippo De Luca (selfrules.org)
     4→**Audit Date:** January 26, 2026
     5→**Subtask:** 2-1 - Apply Platform Selection Scorecard to all candidate platforms
     6→
     7→---
     8→
     9→## Executive Summary
    10→
    11→After applying the Platform Selection Scorecard methodology to all five candidate platforms, **LinkedIn emerges as the clear primary platform** with a score of 9.0/10, significantly ahead of all other options. Twitter/X scores second at 6.4/10, qualifying as a secondary platform worth consideration. Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok all score below the 7.0 threshold and should be deprioritized.
    12→
    13→**Key Recommendation:** Focus 80% of social media effort on LinkedIn, 20% on Twitter/X for extended reach into the global PM community.
    14→
    15→---
    16→
    17→## Scoring Methodology
    18→
    19→### Platform Selection Scorecard Framework
    20→
    21→| Factor | Question | Weight |
    22→|--------|----------|--------|
    23→| **Audience Presence** | Are ideal B2B customers actively using this platform? | 2x |
    24→| **Content Fit** | Does thought leadership content style work here? | 1x |
    25→| **Competitive Gap** | Is there room to stand out vs. other PMs/consultants? | 1x |
    26→| **Resource Match** | Can a solo practitioner consistently create required content? | 1x |
    27→| **Business Alignment** | Does platform support consultation/booking conversions? | 1x |
    28→
    29→**Formula:** `(Audience × 2 + Content + Gap + Resources + Alignment) / 7`
    30→
    31→**Scoring Scale:** 1-10 (1 = Very Poor, 5 = Average, 10 = Excellent)
    32→
    33→**Threshold:** Prioritize platforms scoring 7+. Focus on maximum 2-3 platforms.
    34→
    35→---
    36→
    37→## Platform Scoring: LinkedIn
    38→
    39→### Score: 9.0/10 ⭐ PRIMARY PLATFORM
    40→
    41→| Criterion | Score | Weight | Weighted | Rationale |
    42→|-----------|-------|--------|----------|-----------|
    43→| **Audience Presence** | 10 | 2x | 20 | Perfect B2B fit. Decision-makers, PMs, product leaders ALL on LinkedIn. Italian B2B market has 70%+ LinkedIn penetration for professionals. Target segments (CTOs, CPOs, VPs, PMs) use LinkedIn daily. |
    44→| **Content Fit** | 9 | 1x | 9 | Thought leadership thrives here. Long-form articles, case studies, and professional insights are LinkedIn's core content. The "failure to success" narrative and pragmatic PM advice format is native to the platform. |
    45→| **Competitive Gap** | 8 | 1x | 8 | Moderate competition among PM consultants, but Mattia's unique positioning (design→dev→PM journey) and metrics-backed results differentiate. Italian PM thought leadership space is underserved vs. US market. |
    46→| **Resource Match** | 9 | 1x | 9 | Text-first content is manageable for solo practitioner. LinkedIn allows repurposing blog content, carousel creation from existing materials. 3-4 posts/week is sustainable. |
    47→| **Business Alignment** | 9 | 1x | 9 | Direct path to conversions. Professional context = appropriate for booking consultations. InMail for outreach. Company pages for credibility. LinkedIn profile can link directly to Google Calendar booking. |
    48→
    49→**Calculation:** (10×2 + 9 + 8 + 9 + 9) / 7 = **63 / 7 = 9.0**
    50→
    51→### LinkedIn Platform Analysis
    52→
    53→**Why LinkedIn Scores Highest:**
    54→
    55→1. **Audience-Market Fit**: 100% of target segments (Decision-Makers, Product Teams, Aspiring PMs, Recruiters) are actively on LinkedIn. For Italian B2B, LinkedIn is THE professional network.
    56→
    57→2. **Content Format Alignment**:
    58→   - Long-form posts (1300 characters) suit Mattia's storytelling style
    59→   - Articles for deeper thought leadership pieces
    60→   - Carousels for journey timeline (from website)
    61→   - Polls for engagement content
    62→   - Native video for occasional personal brand content
    63→
    64→3. **Conversion Path**:
    65→   - Profile → Website link → Calendar booking (direct)
    66→   - InMail for high-value prospect engagement
    67→   - Company page for additional credibility
    68→   - Recommendations/endorsements as social proof
    69→
    70→4. **Competition Assessment**:
    71→   - Italian PM space: Low competition, high opportunity
    72→   - Global PM space: High competition but differentiator exists (trilingual journey)
    73→   - Few competitors positioning "failure to success" narrative authentically
    74→
    75→**Current LinkedIn Status:** Active profile, professional certifications displayed, selfrules branding consistent.
    76→
    77→---
    78→
    79→## Platform Scoring: Twitter/X
    80→
    81→### Score: 6.4/10 ⚠️ SECONDARY PLATFORM (CONDITIONAL)
    82→
    83→| Criterion | Score | Weight | Weighted | Rationale |
    84→|-----------|-------|--------|----------|-----------|
    85→| **Audience Presence** | 7 | 2x | 14 | Good PM/tech community presence globally. However, Italian B2B professionals are less active on Twitter than LinkedIn. Aspiring PMs and tech community strong here, but Decision-Makers less so. |
    86→| **Content Fit** | 7 | 1x | 7 | Short insights work well. Thread format allows PM hot-takes and lessons learned. However, requires different content style (punchier, more frequent) than LinkedIn. |
    87→| **Competitive Gap** | 5 | 1x | 5 | High competition. PM Twitter is crowded with thought leaders (Shreyas Doshi, Lenny, etc.). Standing out requires consistent, high-quality content. Italian PM Twitter is smaller, potential niche. |
    88→| **Resource Match** | 6 | 1x | 6 | Higher frequency required (daily vs weekly). Engagement expectations higher. Can repurpose LinkedIn content but requires reformatting. More time investment for same reach. |
    89→| **Business Alignment** | 5 | 1x | 5 | Indirect conversion path. Twitter audience often in "browsing" mode, not "buying" mode. Links to website less clicked. DMs for networking but not standard for B2B sales. |
    90→
    91→**Calculation:** (7×2 + 7 + 5 + 6 + 5) / 7 = **45 / 7 = 6.4**
    92→
    93→### Twitter/X Platform Analysis
    94→
    95→**Why Twitter/X Scores Lower:**
    96→
    97→1. **Audience Fit Gap**: Decision-makers (primary ICP) are less active on Twitter than LinkedIn. While PM/tech community is strong, it skews toward aspiring PMs and tech practitioners rather than buyers.
    98→
    99→2. **Resource Intensity**: Twitter requires more frequent posting (ideally daily) and active engagement (replying, quote-tweeting) to maintain visibility. Algorithm favors consistency.
   100→
   101→3. **Conversion Challenge**: Twitter users are in "content consumption" mode, not "purchase" mode. Booking a consultation from a tweet is a longer journey.
   102→
   103→4. **Competition Reality**: Global PM Twitter is highly competitive. Breaking through requires exceptional content or niche positioning.
   104→
   105→**Conditional Recommendation**: Use Twitter/X for:
   106→- Amplifying LinkedIn content (cross-post insights)
   107→- Engaging with global PM community
   108→- Networking with international prospects
   109→- Testing short-form content ideas
   110→
   111→**Critical Issue:** Handle inconsistency must be resolved first (@Matt_Selfrules vs @mattiadluca).
   112→
   113→---
   114→
   115→## Platform Scoring: Instagram
   116→
   117→### Score: 4.1/10 ❌ NOT RECOMMENDED
   118→
   119→| Criterion | Score | Weight | Weighted | Rationale |
   120→|-----------|-------|--------|----------|-----------|
   121→| **Audience Presence** | 3 | 2x | 6 | Very poor B2B fit. Decision-makers and PMs don't use Instagram for professional content. Platform is primarily B2C, lifestyle, and visual entertainment. Italian B2B audience is not here. |
   122→| **Content Fit** | 5 | 1x | 5 | Visual-first platform conflicts with text-heavy thought leadership. Could work for behind-the-scenes/personal brand, but doesn't align with consulting positioning. |
   123→| **Competitive Gap** | 6 | 1x | 6 | Low competition for PM content (because few PMs are there), but low competition indicates low demand/fit. Name "Mattia De Luca" is crowded by other profiles. |
   124→| **Resource Match** | 3 | 1x | 3 | High production effort required. Quality photos/graphics/reels needed. Solo practitioner cannot maintain quality cadence alongside LinkedIn focus. |
   125→| **Business Alignment** | 2 | 1x | 2 | No path to B2B conversions. Instagram users are not booking consulting calls. Platform doesn't support professional services discovery. Link-in-bio friction is high. |
   126→
   127→**Calculation:** (3×2 + 5 + 6 + 3 + 2) / 7 = **29 / 7 = 4.1**
   128→
   129→### Instagram Platform Analysis
   130→
   131→**Why Instagram Should Be Deprioritized:**
   132→
   133→1. **Fundamental Misalignment**: Instagram is a B2C, lifestyle, visual-entertainment platform. B2B professional services don't convert here.
   134→
   135→2. **Content Mismatch**: Mattia's value is in insights, frameworks, and professional guidance - all text-heavy content that Instagram deprioritizes.
   136→
   137→3. **Resource Drain**: Creating quality visual content (carousels, reels, stories) requires significant time investment that would be better spent on LinkedIn.
   138→
   139→4. **Zero Conversion Path**: There's no natural journey from Instagram → Consultation booking for B2B services.
   140→
   141→**Exception Case**: Only consider if pursuing personal brand expansion into lifestyle/creator economy (not current business model).
   142→
   143→---
   144→
   145→## Platform Scoring: YouTube
   146→
   147→### Score: 4.7/10 ❌ NOT RECOMMENDED (NOW)
   148→
   149→| Criterion | Score | Weight | Weighted | Rationale |
   150→|-----------|-------|--------|----------|-----------|
   151→| **Audience Presence** | 5 | 2x | 10 | Moderate presence. PM content exists on YouTube, but it's not where B2B buyers discover consultants. More educational/tutorial audience than purchasing decision-makers. |
   152→| **Content Fit** | 6 | 1x | 6 | Long-form video could work for PM tutorials, case studies, interviews. However, requires significant production shift from current tex

     5→This task involves conducting a comprehensive social media strategy analysis for selfrules.org, the personal brand website of Mattia Filippo De Luca, a Product Manager with 13 years of experience offering B2B professional services (consulting, brainstorming, PM mentorship). The audit will evaluate current social presence, identify the optimal primary platform, develop a 30-day content plan, and create a community-focused engagement strategy that prioritizes meaningful relationships over vanity metrics.
     6→
     7→## Workflow Type
     8→
     9→**Type**: feature
    10→
    11→**Rationale**: This is a strategic deliverable task that requires comprehensive analysis, framework application, and creation of actionable artifacts (audit report, content calendar, engagement playbook). While not a code implementation, it follows the feature workflow pattern of research → analysis → deliverable creation → validation.
    12→
    13→## Task Scope
    14→
    15→### Services Involved
    16→- **main** (primary) - Website analysis for social integration assessment
    17→- **social-media-manager skill** (framework) - Strategic analysis methodologies
    18→
    19→### This Task Will:
    20→- [ ] Analyze all current social media channels with quantified scoring
    21→- [ ] Evaluate bidirectional website-social integration
    22→- [ ] Identify and recommend the #1 priority platform with data-driven rationale
    23→- [ ] Create a 30-day cross-platform content calendar
    24→- [ ] Develop a community building engagement strategy (not follower acquisition)
    25→- [ ] Apply REACH metrics and TRIBE community frameworks
    26→- [ ] Generate actionable recommendations prioritized by impact/effort
    27→
    28→### Out of Scope:
    29→- Actual social media post creation (use copywriter-hybrid agent for that)
    30→- Social media account setup or configuration
    31→- Automated posting integrations or API development
    32→- Paid advertising strategy
    33→- Influencer partnership recommendations

    36→
    37→### Main Website (selfrules.org)

    69→- Platform-specific strategy deep dives

    89→| File | Pattern to Copy |
    90→|------|----------------|

    97→## Patterns to Follow
    98→
    99→### Platform Selection Scorecard
   100→
   101→From `.claude/skills/social-media-manager/SKILL.md`:
   102→
   103→| Factor | Question | Weight |
   104→|--------|----------|--------|
   105→| **Audience Presence** | Are ideal customers actively using this platform? | 2x |
   106→| **Content Fit** | Does natural content style work here? | 1x |
   107→| **Competitive Gap** | Is there room to stand out vs. competitors? | 1x |
   108→| **Resource Match** | Can you consistently create required content? | 1x |
   109→| **Business Alignment** | Does platform support conversion goals? | 1x |
   110→
   111→**Score Formula:** `(Audience × 2 + Content + Gap + Resources + Alignment) / 7`

   131→| **I**nvest | Deliver consistent value | Exclusive content, recognition |
   132→| **B**ond | Create member connections | Discussions, collaborations |

   140→| Engagement Posts | 25% | Questions, polls, discussions |
   141→| Promotional Posts | 15% | CTAs, offers, conversions |
   142→
   143→## Requirements

   146→
   147→1. **Social Presence Audit**

   180→RICE vs ICE: which prioritization framework I actually use after 13 years as PM.
   181→
   182→Spoiler: neither.
   183→
   184→Here's why both frameworks fail in practice:
   185→
   186→RICE (Reach × Impact × Confidence / Effort):
   187→✅ Great for data-driven teams
   188→❌ "Confidence" becomes a political number
   189→❌ Teams game the scores to get their features prioritized
   190→
   191→ICE (Impact × Confidence × Ease):
   192→✅ Simpler, faster
   193→❌ Same "Confidence" problem
   194→❌ Ignores reach completely
   195→
   196→What I actually use: The "Regret Minimization" Filter
   197→
   198→For every feature request, I ask:
   199→"If we don't ship this in 6 months, will we regret it?"
   200→
   201→• If yes → goes to top of backlog
   202→• If no → goes to "maybe later" pile
   203→• If "it depends" → needs more discovery
   204→
   205→This question cuts through all the gaming and politics.
   206→
   207→What prioritization method actually works for your team?
   208→
   209→—
   210→
   211→#ProductManagement #prioritization #PM #agile

1→# TRIBE Community Building Strategy for selfrules.org

     3→**Subject:** Mattia Filippo De Luca (selfrules.org)
     4→**Audit Date:** January 26, 2026
     5→**Subtask:** 3-3 - Apply TRIBE model for community building strategy
     6→**Framework:** TRIBE Community Model (Target, Recruit, Invest, Bond, Empower)
     7→
     8→---
     9→
    10→## Executive Summary
    11→
    12→This document applies the **TRIBE Community Model** to build an engaged professional community around Mattia's Product Management expertise. The strategy focuses on **community quality over follower quantity**, aligning with the B2B professional services business model.
    13→
    14→### TRIBE Model Overview
    15→
    16→```
    17→THE TRIBE COMMUNITY BUILDING FRAMEWORK
    18→═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    19→
    20→  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    21→  │                                                                     │
    22→  │   T ─────► R ─────► I ─────► B ─────► E                            │
    23→  │   │        │        │        │        │                            │
    24→  │   ▼        ▼        ▼        ▼        ▼                            │
    25→  │ TARGET  RECRUIT  INVEST   BOND    EMPOWER                          │
    26→  │                                                                     │
    27→  │ Define   Attract  Deliver  Create   Turn                           │
    28→  │ ideal    right    value    member   members                        │
    29→  │ member   people   + care   bonds    into                           │
    30→  │                                     advocates                       │
    31→  │                                                                     │
    32→  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    33→
    34→  Goal: Build a community of engaged PM professionals who know, like,
    35→        and trust Mattia - not just follow counts.
    36→
    37→═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    38→```
    39→
    40→### Key Metrics Focus (Anti-Vanity)
    41→
    42→| Vanity Metric (Avoid) | Community Metric (Track) |
    43→|-----------------------|--------------------------|
    44→| Follower count | Active commenters per post |
    45→| Impressions | Comment quality & depth |
    46→| Post views | Profile-to-booking ratio |
    47→| Likes | Return engagers (repeat commenters) |
    48→| Connection requests | Meaningful DM conversations |
    49→
    50→---
    51→
    52→## Phase T: TARGET - Define Ideal Community Member
    53→
    54→**Goal:** Clearly define who belongs in the community and who doesn't. This clarity enables all subsequent phases to be more effective.
    55→
    56→### 3 Primary Community Personas
    57→
    58→Based on the target audience profile analysis, the ideal community members are:
    59→
    60→#### Persona 1: "The Overwhelmed PM Leader"
    61→
    62→| Attribute | Description |
    63→|-----------|-------------|
    64→| **Title** | CTO, CPO, VP Product, Head of Product |
    65→| **Company** | B2B SaaS or Enterprise Software, 50-500 employees |
    66→| **Location** | Italy (primary), EU (secondary), Remote-friendly (tertiary) |
    67→| **Pain Point** | Cross-functional chaos, roadmap overwhelm, alignment theater |
    68→| **Content Need** | Strategic insights, battle-tested frameworks, executive perspective |
    69→| **Community Value** | Peer benchmarking, executive-level discussions, trusted advisor access |
    70→| **Conversion Goal** | Consulting service (€2K-5K sessions) |
    71→
    72→**Identification Signals:**
    73→- Posts about leadership challenges, scaling teams, strategic decisions
    74→- Engages with content about organization design, product strategy
    75→- Uses phrases like "alignment," "roadmap chaos," "stakeholder management"
    76→- Shares hiring content for senior PM roles
    77→
    78→---
    79→
    80→#### Persona 2: "The Execution-Focused PM"
    81→
    82→| Attribute | Description |
    83→|-----------|-------------|
    84→| **Title** | Product Manager, Senior PM, Product Owner, Team Lead |
    85→| **Company** | Tech startup or scale-up, 10-200 employees |
    86→| **Location** | Italy, EU, Global remote |
    87→| **Pain Point** | Stakeholder overwhelm, prioritization paralysis, cross-functional friction |
    88→| **Content Need** | Practical how-tos, meeting tactics, prioritization frameworks |
    89→| **Community Value** | Peer support, tactical advice, skill development |
    90→| **Conversion Goal** | Brainstorming service (€500-2K sessions) |
    91→
    92→**Identification Signals:**
    93→- Posts about sprint challenges, backlog management, feature prioritization
    94→- Asks tactical questions in comments ("How do you handle...?")
    95→- Shares wins and struggles from day-to-day PM work
    96→- Engages with Agile/Scrum content
    97→
    98→---
    99→
   100→#### Persona 3: "The Aspiring PM"
   101→
   102→| Attribute | Description |
   103→|-----------|-------------|
   104→| **Title** | Junior PM, Associate PM, Designer-to-PM, Developer-to-PM, Project Manager |
   105→| **Company** | Any (often early-stage career at smaller companies) |
   106→| **Location** | Italy, Global (strong English segment) |
   107→| **Pain Point** | Career transition uncertainty, skill gaps, imposter syndrome |

   109→| **Community Value** | Mentorship access, career guidance, inspirational stories |
   110→| **Conversion Goal** | Mentorship service (€200-500/month) |
   111→
   112→**Identification Signals:**
   113→- Posts about career transitions, job searching, interview prep
   114→- Asks questions about PM career paths, certifications, skills
   115→- Engages with "lessons learned" and "failure stories" content
   116→- Follows PM thought leaders and course creators
   117→
   118→---
   119→
   120→### Community Exclusion Criteria
   121→
   122→**NOT the ideal community member:**
   123→
   124→| Type | Why Exclude | How to Identify |
   125→|------|-------------|-----------------|
   126→| Passive lurkers with no engagement intent | No community contribution | Never comment, just view |
   127→| Job spammers | Distract from value focus | Only post job links, no discussion |
   128→| Aggressive self-promoters | Extract value without giving | Every comment links to their product |
   129→| Non-PM roles with no adjacent interest | Topic mismatch | Engage only to sell unrelated services |
   130→
   131→**Boundary Tactics:**
   132→- Focus engagement on commenters who add value to discussions
   133→- Politely redirect off-topic promoters in DMs
   134→- Don't respond to spam or low-effort comments
   135→- Nurture high-quality commenters with personalized responses
   136→

   138→
   139→### Actionable Tactics for TARGET Phase

   141→| # | Tactic | Action | Frequency | Time Investment |

   143→| T1 | **Persona Review** | Review and refine community personas quarterly | Quarterly | 1 hr |
   144→| T2 | **Profile Scanning** | Check profiles of top commenters to understand who resonates | Weekly | 15 min |
   145→| T3 | **Comment Pattern Analysis** | Track which posts attract target personas vs. non-targets | Monthly | 30 min |
   146→| T4 | **Hashtag Monitoring** | Follow #ProductManagement, #PM, #prodmgmt to find target personas | Daily | 5 min |
   147→| T5 | **Competitor Audience Analysis** | Identify followers of other PM thought leaders who match personas | Monthly | 30 min |
   148→
   149→---
   150→
   151→## Phase R: RECRUIT - Attract the Right People
   152→
   153→**Goal:** Use valuable content and strategic engagement to attract ideal community members—not random followers.
   154→
   155→### Content Strategy for Recruitment
   156→
   157→Content is the primary recruitment vehicle. Each content pillar should attract specific personas:

1→# Platform Selection Scorecard Results
     2→
     3→**Subject:** Mattia Filippo De Luca (selfrules.org)
     4→**Audit Date:** January 26, 2026
     5→**Subtask:** 2-1 - Apply Platform Selection Scorecard to all candidate platforms
     6→
     7→---
     8→
     9→## Executive Summary
    10→
    11→After applying the Platform Selection Scorecard methodology to all five candidate platforms, **LinkedIn emerges as the clear primary platform** with a score of 9.0/10, significantly ahead of all other options. Twitter/X scores second at 6.4/10, qualifying as a secondary platform worth consideration. Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok all score below the 7.0 threshold and should be deprioritized.
    12→
    13→**Key Recommendation:** Focus 80% of social media effort on LinkedIn, 20% on Twitter/X for extended reach into the global PM community.
    14→
    15→---
    16→
    17→## Scoring Methodology
    18→
    19→### Platform Selection Scorecard Framework
    20→
    21→| Factor | Question | Weight |
    22→|--------|----------|--------|
    23→| **Audience Presence** | Are ideal B2B customers actively using this platform? | 2x |
    24→| **Content Fit** | Does thought leadership content style work here? | 1x |
    25→| **Competitive Gap** | Is there room to stand out vs. other PMs/consultants? | 1x |
    26→| **Resource Match** | Can a solo practitioner consistently create required content? | 1x |
    27→| **Business Alignment** | Does platform support consultation/booking conversions? | 1x |
    28→
    29→**Formula:** `(Audience × 2 + Content + Gap + Resources + Alignment) / 7`
    30→
    31→**Scoring Scale:** 1-10 (1 = Very Poor, 5 = Average, 10 = Excellent)
    32→
    33→**Threshold:** Prioritize platforms scoring 7+. Focus on maximum 2-3 platforms.
    34→
    35→---
    36→
    37→## Platform Scoring: LinkedIn
    38→
    39→### Score: 9.0/10 ⭐ PRIMARY PLATFORM
    40→
    41→| Criterion | Score | Weight | Weighted | Rationale |
    42→|-----------|-------|--------|----------|-----------|
    43→| **Audience Presence** | 10 | 2x | 20 | Perfect B2B fit. Decision-makers, PMs, product leaders ALL on LinkedIn. Italian B2B market has 70%+ LinkedIn penetration for professionals. Target segments (CTOs, CPOs, VPs, PMs) use LinkedIn daily. |
    44→| **Content Fit** | 9 | 1x | 9 | Thought leadership thrives here. Long-form articles, case studies, and professional insights are LinkedIn's core content. The "failure to success" narrative and pragmatic PM advice format is native to the platform. |
    45→| **Competitive Gap** | 8 | 1x | 8 | Moderate competition among PM consultants, but Mattia's unique positioning (design→dev→PM journey) and metrics-backed results differentiate. Italian PM thought leadership space is underserved vs. US market. |
    46→| **Resource Match** | 9 | 1x | 9 | Text-first content is manageable for solo practitioner. LinkedIn allows repurposing blog content, carousel creation from existing materials. 3-4 posts/week is sustainable. |
    47→| **Business Alignment** | 9 | 1x | 9 | Direct path to conversions. Professional context = appropriate for booking consultations. InMail for outreach. Company pages for credibility. LinkedIn profile can link directly to Google Calendar booking. |
    48→
    49→**Calculation:** (10×2 + 9 + 8 + 9 + 9) / 7 = **63 / 7 = 9.0**
    50→
    51→### LinkedIn Platform Analysis
    52→
    53→**Why LinkedIn Scores Highest:**
    54→
    55→1. **Audience-Market Fit**: 100% of target segments (Decision-Makers, Product Teams, Aspiring PMs, Recruiters) are actively on LinkedIn. For Italian B2B, LinkedIn is THE professional network.
    56→
    57→2. **Content Format Alignment**:
    58→   - Long-form posts (1300 characters) suit Mattia's storytelling style
    59→   - Articles for deeper thought leadership pieces
    60→   - Carousels for journey timeline (from website)
    61→   - Polls for engagement content
    62→   - Native video for occasional personal brand content
    63→
    64→3. **Conversion Path**:
    65→   - Profile → Website link → Calendar booking (direct)
    66→   - InMail for high-value prospect engagement
    67→   - Company page for additional credibility
    68→   - Recommendations/endorsements as social proof
    69→
    70→4. **Competition Assessment**:
    71→   - Italian PM space: Low competition, high opportunity
    72→   - Global PM space: High competition but differentiator exists (trilingual journey)
    73→   - Few competitors positioning "failure to success" narrative authentically
    74→
    75→**Current LinkedIn Status:** Active profile, professional certifications displayed, selfrules branding consistent.
    76→
    77→---
    78→
    79→## Platform Scoring: Twitter/X
    80→
    81→### Score: 6.4/10 ⚠️ SECONDARY PLATFORM (CONDITIONAL)
    82→
    83→| Criterion | Score | Weight | Weighted | Rationale |
    84→|-----------|-------|--------|----------|-----------|
    85→| **Audience Presence** | 7 | 2x | 14 | Good PM/tech community presence globally. However, Italian B2B professionals are less active on Twitter than LinkedIn. Aspiring PMs and tech community strong here, but Decision-Makers less so. |
    86→| **Content Fit** | 7 | 1x | 7 | Short insights work well. Thread format allows PM hot-takes and lessons learned. However, requires different content style (punchier, more frequent) than LinkedIn. |
    87→| **Competitive Gap** | 5 | 1x | 5 | High competition. PM Twitter is crowded with thought leaders (Shreyas Doshi, Lenny, etc.). Standing out requires consistent, high-quality content. Italian PM Twitter is smaller, potential niche. |
    88→| **Resource Match** | 6 | 1x | 6 | Higher frequency required (daily vs weekly). Engagement expectations higher. Can repurpose LinkedIn content but requires reformatting. More time investment for same reach. |
    89→| **Business Alignment** | 5 | 1x | 5 | Indirect conversion path. Twitter audience often in "browsing" mode, not "buying" mode. Links to website less clicked. DMs for networking but not standard for B2B sales. |
    90→
    91→**Calculation:** (7×2 + 7 + 5 + 6 + 5) / 7 = **45 / 7 = 6.4**
    92→
    93→### Twitter/X Platform Analysis
    94→
    95→**Why Twitter/X Scores Lower:**
    96→
    97→1. **Audience Fit Gap**: Decision-makers (primary ICP) are less active on Twitter than LinkedIn. While PM/tech community is strong, it skews toward aspiring PMs and tech practitioners rather than buyers.
    98→
    99→2. **Resource Intensity**: Twitter requires more frequent posting (ideally daily) and active engagement (replying, quote-tweeting) to maintain visibility. Algorithm favors consistency.
   100→
   101→3. **Conversion Challenge**: Twitter users are in "content consumption" mode, not "purchase" mode. Booking a consultation from a tweet is a longer journey.
   102→
   103→4. **Competition Reality**: Global PM Twitter is highly competitive. Breaking through requires exceptional content or niche positioning.
   104→
   105→**Conditional Recommendation**: Use Twitter/X for:
   106→- Amplifying LinkedIn content (cross-post insights)
   107→- Engaging with global PM community
   108→- Networking with international prospects
   109→- Testing short-form content ideas
   110→
   111→**Critical Issue:** Handle inconsistency must be resolved first (@Matt_Selfrules vs @mattiadluca).
   112→
   113→---
   114→
   115→## Platform Scoring: Instagram
   116→
   117→### Score: 4.1/10 ❌ NOT RECOMMENDED
   118→
   119→| Criterion | Score | Weight | Weighted | Rationale |
   120→|-----------|-------|--------|----------|-----------|
   121→| **Audience Presence** | 3 | 2x | 6 | Very poor B2B fit. Decision-makers and PMs don't use Instagram for professional content. Platform is primarily B2C, lifestyle, and visual entertainment. Italian B2B audience is not here. |
   122→| **Content Fit** | 5 | 1x | 5 | Visual-first platform conflicts with text-heavy thought leadership. Could work for behind-the-scenes/personal brand, but doesn't align with consulting positioning. |
   123→| **Competitive Gap** | 6 | 1x | 6 | Low competition for PM content (because few PMs are there), but low competition indicates low demand/fit. Name "Mattia De Luca" is crowded by other profiles. |
   124→| **Resource Match** | 3 | 1x | 3 | High production effort required. Quality photos/graphics/reels needed. Solo practitioner cannot maintain quality cadence alongside LinkedIn focus. |
   125→| **Business Alignment** | 2 | 1x | 2 | No path to B2B conversions. Instagram users are not booking consulting calls. Platform doesn't support professional services discovery. Link-in-bio friction is high. |
   126→
   127→**Calculation:** (3×2 + 5 + 6 + 3 + 2) / 7 = **29 / 7 = 4.1**
   128→
   129→### Instagram Platform Analysis
   130→
   131→**Why Instagram Should Be Deprioritized:**
   132→
   133→1. **Fundamental Misalignment**: Instagram is a B2C, lifestyle, visual-entertainment platform. B2B professional services don't convert here.
   134→
   135→2. **Content Mismatch**: Mattia's value is in insights, frameworks, and professional guidance - all text-heavy content that Instagram deprioritizes.
   136→
   137→3. **Resource Drain**: Creating quality visual content (carousels, reels, stories) requires significant time investment that would be better spent on LinkedIn.
   138→
   139→4. **Zero Conversion Path**: There's no natural journey from Instagram → Consultation booking for B2B services.
   140→
   141→**Exception Case**: Only consider if pursuing personal brand expansion into lifestyle/creator economy (not current business model).
   142→

   145→## Platform Scoring: YouTube

   147→### Score: 4.7/10 ❌ NOT RECOMMENDED (NOW)

     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→This task involves conducting a comprehensive social media strategy analysis for selfrules.org, the personal brand website of Mattia Filippo De Luca, a Product Manager with 13 years of experience offering B2B professional services (consulting, brainstorming, PM mentorship). The audit will evaluate current social presence, identify the optimal primary platform, develop a 30-day content plan, and create a community-focused engagement strategy that prioritizes meaningful relationships over vanity metrics.
     6→
     7→## Workflow Type
     8→
     9→**Type**: feature
    10→

While not a code implementation, it follows the feature workflow pattern of research → analysis → deliverable creation → validation.
    12→

    22→- [ ] Identify and recommend the #1 priority platform with data-driven rationale
    23→- [ ] Create a 30-day cross-platform content calendar
    24→- [ ] Develop a community building engagement strategy (not follower acquisition)
    25→- [ ] Apply REACH metrics and TRIBE community frameworks
    26→- [ ] Generate actionable recommendations prioritized by impact/effort
    27→
    28→### Out of Scope:
    29→- Actual social media post creation (use copywriter-hybrid agent for that)

    31→- Automated posting integrations or API development
    32→- Paid advertising strategy
    33→- Influencer partnership recommendations

   161→   - Acceptance: Daily/weekly schedule covering all recommended platforms with content types
   162→
   163→5. **Community Engagement Strategy**
   164→   - Description: Framework for building engaged community (not just follower acquisition)

   166→
   167→### Edge Cases

   169→1. **Limited Social Presence** - If few/no active social accounts exist, focus on greenfield strategy and platform launch recommendations
   170→2. **Bilingual Audience** - Address Italian/English content split strategy for international reach
   171→3. **B2B vs B2C Balance** - Professional services audience requires LinkedIn-first approach but may benefit from broader reach
   172→4. **Time/Resource Constraints** - Solo practitioner means realistic, sustainable content cadence recommendations
   173→
   174→## Implementation Notes
   175→
   176→### DO
   177→- Apply Platform Selection Scorecard with actual scores for each platform
   178→- Use REACH metrics framework to define KPIs
   179→- Focus on community building (TRIBE model) over follower counts

1→# Specification: Social Media Strategy Audit for selfrules.org
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→This task involves conducting a comprehensive social media strategy analysis for selfrules.org, the personal brand website of Mattia Filippo De Luca, a Product Manager with 13 years of experience offering B2B professional services (consulting, brainstorming, PM mentorship). The audit will evaluate current social presence, identify the optimal primary platform, develop a 30-day content plan, and create a community-focused engagement strategy that prioritizes meaningful relationships over vanity metrics.
     6→
     7→## Workflow Type
     8→
     9→**Type**: feature
    10→
    11→**Rationale**: This is a strategic deliverable task that requires comprehensive analysis, framework application, and creation of actionable artifacts (audit report, content calendar, engagement playbook). While not a code implementation, it follows the feature workflow pattern of research → analysis → deliverable creation → validation.
    12→
    13→## Task Scope
    14→
    15→### Services Involved
    16→- **main** (primary) - Website analysis for social integration assessment
    17→- **social-media-manager skill** (framework) - Strategic analysis methodologies
    18→
    19→### This Task Will:
    20→- [ ] Analyze all current social media channels with quantified scoring
    21→- [ ] Evaluate bidirectional website-social integration
    22→- [ ] Identify and recommend the #1 priority platform with data-driven rationale
    23→- [ ] Create a 30-day cross-platform content calendar
    24→- [ ] Develop a community building engagement strategy (not follower acquisition)
    25→- [ ] Apply REACH metrics and TRIBE community frameworks
    26→- [ ] Generate actionable recommendations prioritized by impact/effort
    27→
    28→### Out of Scope:
    29→- Actual social media post creation (use copywriter-hybrid agent for that)
    30→- Social media account setup or configuration
    31→- Automated posting integrations or API development
    32→- Paid advertising strategy
    33→- Influencer partnership recommendations
    34→
    35→## Service Context
    36→
    37→### Main Website (selfrules.org)
    38→
    39→**Tech Stack:**
    40→- Language: TypeScript
    41→- Framework: Next.js 14 (App Router)
    42→- Styling: Tailwind CSS (Neobrutalist design system)
    43→- Key directories: app, components, lib
    44→
    45→**Entry Point:** `app/[locale]/page.tsx`
    46→
    47→**How to Run:**
    48→```bash
    49→npm run dev
    50→```
    51→
    52→**Port:** 3000
    53→
    54→**Relevant Sections for Social Integration:**
    55→- Homepage hero and CTAs
    56→- Blog section
    57→- Contact/Booking section
    58→- Footer social links
    59→
    60→### Social Media Manager Skill
    61→
    62→**Location:** `.claude/skills/social-media-manager/SKILL.md`
    63→
    64→**Key Frameworks Available:**
    65→- Platform Selection Scorecard (1-10 rating system)
    66→- REACH Metrics Model (Reach, Engagement, Amplification, Conversion, Holding)
    67→- TRIBE Community Model (Target, Recruit, Invest, Bond, Empower)
    68→- 4-1-1 Content Mix Rule (60% value, 25% engagement, 15% promotional)
    69→- Platform-specific strategy deep dives
    70→
    71→## Files to Modify
    72→
    73→| File | Service | What to Change |
    74→|------|---------|---------------|
    75→| N/A - Strategic deliverable | N/A | Create audit report document |
    76→
    77→**Output Deliverables:**
    78→| Deliverable | Format | Description |
    79→|-------------|--------|-------------|
    80→| Social Audit Report | Markdown | Comprehensive analysis with scores |
    81→| Platform Recommendation | Analysis | #1 platform with rationale |
    82→| 30-Day Content Calendar | Table/Schedule | Cross-platform content plan |
    83→| Engagement Playbook | Framework | Community building strategy |
    84→
    85→## Files to Reference
    86→
    87→These files provide context and frameworks:
    88→
    89→| File | Pattern to Copy |
    90→|------|----------------|
    91→| `.claude/skills/social-media-manager/SKILL.md` | Platform Selection Scorecard, REACH metrics, TRIBE model |
    92→| `.claude/skills/marketing-manager/SKILL.md` | AARRR Pirate Metrics, growth loops |
    93→| `.claude/skills/web-analyst/SKILL.md` | HEART framework for site integration |

    97→## Patterns to Follow
    98→
    99→### Platform Selection Scorecard
   100→
   101→From `.claude/skills/social-media-manager/SKILL.md`:
   102→
   103→| Factor | Question | Weight |
   104→|--------|----------|--------|
   105→| **Audience Presence** | Are ideal customers actively using this platform? | 2x |
   106→| **Content Fit** | Does natural content style work here? | 1x |
   107→| **Competitive Gap** | Is there room to stand out vs. competitors? | 1x |
   108→| **Resource Match** | Can you consistently create required content? | 1x |
   109→| **Business Alignment** | Does platform support conversion goals? | 1x |
   110→
   111→**Score Formula:** `(Audience × 2 + Content + Gap + Resources + Alignment) / 7`
   112→
   113→**Threshold:** Prioritize platforms scoring 7+. Focus on 2-3 maximum.
   114→
   115→### REACH Metrics Model
   116→
   117→| Metric | Definition | Business Value |
   118→|--------|------------|----------------|
   119→| **R**each | Unique accounts who saw content | Awareness, top-of-funnel |
   120→| **E**ngagement | Interactions / reach | Content resonance |
   121→| **A**mplification | Shares, retweets, reposts | Organic distribution |
   122→| **C**onversion | Clicks, profile visits, follows | Action-taking |
   123→| **H**olding | Watch time, dwell time | Content quality |

     5→This task involves conducting a comprehensive social media strategy analysis for selfrules.org, the personal brand website of Mattia Filippo De Luca, a Product Manager with 13 years of experience offering B2B professional services (consulting, brainstorming, PM mentorship). The audit will evaluate current social presence, identify the optimal primary platform, develop a 30-day content plan, and create a community-focused engagement strategy that prioritizes meaningful relationships over vanity metrics.
     6→

     8→
     9→**Type**: feature
    10→
    11→**Rationale**: This is a strategic deliverable task that requires comprehensive analysis, framework application, and creation of actionable artifacts (audit report, content calendar, engagement playbook). While not a code implementation, it follows the feature workflow pattern of research → analysis → deliverable creation → validation.
    12→
    13→## Task Scope

    22→- [ ] Identify and recommend the #1 priority platform with data-driven rationale
    23→- [ ] Create a 30-day cross-platform content calendar
    24→- [ ] Develop a community building engagement strategy (not follower acquisition)
    25→- [ ] Apply REACH metrics and TRIBE community frameworks
    26→- [ ] Generate actionable recommendations prioritized by impact/effort
    27→
    28→### Out of Scope:
    29→- Actual social media post creation (use copywriter-hybrid agent for that)
    30→- Social media account setup or configuration
    31→- Automated posting integrations or API development
    32→- Paid advertising strategy
    33→- Influencer partnership recommendations
    34→
    35→## Service Context

    53→

    55→- Homepage hero and CTAs

    58→- Footer social links

    60→### Social Media Manager Skill
    61→

    64→**Key Frameworks Available:**

    67→- TRIBE Community Model (Target, Recruit, Invest, Bond, Empower)

    97→## Patterns to Follow

    99→### Platform Selection Scorecard

1→# REACH Metrics & KPI Framework for selfrules.org
     2→
     3→**Subject:** Mattia Filippo De Luca (selfrules.org)
     4→**Audit Date:** January 26, 2026
     5→**Subtask:** 3-4 - Define REACH metrics and KPIs per platform
     6→**Framework:** REACH Metrics Model (Reach, Engagement, Amplification, Conversion, Holding)
     7→
     8→---
     9→
    10→## Executive Summary
    11→
    12→This document defines the **REACH Metrics Framework** for measuring social media success for selfrules.org. The framework prioritizes **community quality over vanity metrics**, aligning with the B2B professional services business model. Each metric is defined with platform-specific targets, measurement methods, and actionable benchmarks.
    13→
    14→### REACH Framework Overview
    15→
    16→```
    17→THE REACH METRICS MODEL
    18→===============================================================================
    19→
    20→  R ─────► E ─────► A ─────► C ─────► H
    21→  │        │        │        │        │
    22→  ▼        ▼        ▼        ▼        ▼
    23→REACH   ENGAGE   AMPLIFY  CONVERT   HOLD
    24→
    25→Unique   Quality   Organic  Profile   Dwell
    26→viewers  interact  shares   visits    time
    27→         (NOT      reposts  clicks    retention
    28→          likes)            bookings
    29→
    30→===============================================================================
    31→
    32→Business Value Flow:
    33→REACH (Awareness) → ENGAGEMENT (Resonance) → AMPLIFICATION (Distribution)
    34→→ CONVERSION (Action) → HOLDING (Loyalty)
    35→
    36→```
    37→
    38→### Anti-Vanity Metrics Commitment
    39→
    40→| Vanity Metric (AVOID) | Community Metric (TRACK) | Why |
    41→|-----------------------|--------------------------|-----|
    42→| Follower count | Active commenters per post | Followers ≠ customers |
    43→| Total impressions | Quality reach to target personas | Impressions ≠ engagement |
    44→| Likes count | Comment depth & quality | Likes = low effort, no intent |
    45→| Post views | Profile-to-booking ratio | Views ≠ interest |
    46→| Connection count | Meaningful DM conversations | Connections ≠ relationships |
    47→
    48→---
    49→
    50→## REACH Metric #1: REACH (R)
    51→
    52→### Definition
    53→
    54→**Reach** measures the **unique accounts who saw your content**. It represents awareness and top-of-funnel visibility. However, raw reach is meaningless without context—we focus on **qualified reach** to target personas.
    55→
    56→### Business Value
    57→
    58→| Stage | Purpose |
    59→|-------|---------|
    60→| Funnel Position | Top-of-funnel (TOFU) |
    61→| Business Goal | Awareness building among target segments |
    62→| What It Signals | Content visibility within target audience |
    63→| What It Doesn't Signal | Interest, intent, or conversion likelihood |
    64→
    65→### Platform-Specific Metrics
    66→
    67→#### LinkedIn (Primary Platform)
    68→
    69→| Metric | Definition | How to Track |
    70→|--------|------------|--------------|
    71→| **Post Impressions** | Total views of a post | LinkedIn Analytics → Posts → Impressions |
    72→| **Unique Viewers** | Distinct accounts that saw post | LinkedIn Analytics → Unique impressions |
    73→| **Profile Views** | Users who visited profile | LinkedIn → Analytics → Profile views |
    74→| **Discovery Rate** | % impressions from non-followers | LinkedIn → Post details → Discovery |
    75→
    76→#### Twitter/X (Secondary Platform)
    77→
    78→| Metric | Definition | How to Track |
    79→|--------|------------|--------------|
    80→| **Impressions** | Total times tweet appeared in feeds | Twitter Analytics → Tweet activity |
    81→| **Profile Visits** | Users who clicked through to profile | Twitter Analytics → 28-day summary |
    82→| **Follower Reach %** | % of followers who saw tweet | Impressions / Follower count |
    83→
    84→### Target Benchmarks
    85→
    86→#### LinkedIn REACH Targets
    87→

Twitter/X scores second at 6.4/10, qualifying as a secondary platform worth consideration. Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok all score below the 7.0 threshold and should be deprioritized.
